questions.text:
Consider the following Syntax Directed Translation Scheme(SDTS),with non-terminals {S, A} and terminals {a, b}.
S [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] aA {print 1}
S [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] a { print 2}
A [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Sb { print 3}
Using the above SDTS, the output printed by a bottom-up parser, for the input aab is:
questions.solution:
Parse aab bottom-up:
1. The second a is reduced by [latex]S\rightarrow a[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] prints 2
2. S b is reduced by [latex]A\rightarrow Sb[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] prints 3
3. a A is reduced by [latex]S\rightarrow aA[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] prints 1

Answer: 231

questions.text:
Consider the following code segment.
x =u-t;
y =x*v;
x =y+w;
y =t-z;
y =x*y;
The minimum number of total variables required to convert the above code segment to static single assignment form is__________ .
questions.solution:
In SSA form every assignment gets a new variable:
[latex]x_1=u-t;\ y_1=x_1v;\ x_2=y_1+w;\ y_2=t-z;\ y_3=x_2y_2[/latex]

New variables: [latex]x_1,y_1,x_2,y_2,y_3[/latex] (5), plus the inputs u, t, v, w, z (5).

Total = 10

Answer: 10

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

An SLR table has no conflicts, so the grammar must be unambiguous. But some unambiguous grammars are not SLR (they are LALR or LR(1)).

- Canonical LR is the most powerful, not LALR.
- LR(k) parsing does not backtrack.

Answer: Every SLR grammar is unambiguous but not every unambiguous grammar is SLR
